Thomas More, a prominent figure in the 16th century, is known for his letter to Ulrich von Hutten, which is often referred to as "the first real biography in the real modern sense." His writing method, as described in De copia and De ratio studii, involved making notes on various themes from his readings, categorizing them in boxes that he carried with him. When composing a new book, he would go through these commonplace notes, cross out the ones he used, and weave together new works from the same topics. This catalog of research notes allowed him to write books quickly.

Regarding the virus, it enters the cell by way of an endosome. Once inside, the virus utilizes the acidic environment of the endosome and binds to its membrane simultaneously, releasing its five proteins and single-strand RNA into the cytoplasm. Within a muscle or nerve cell, the virus replicates. The L protein then transcribes five mRNA strands and a positive strand of RNA from the original negative-strand RNA using free nucleotides in the cytoplasm. These five mRNA strands are then used for protein synthesis.
